hook_text: A spaza owner needs to lift 50 kilogram bags onto a shelf. Do not sketch yet. Find out first.
clip_script: Facts first. Load: 50 kilograms, about 500 newtons. Height: 900 millimetres. Twenty times a week. Who: the owner, not strong, children around. Where: a small room, narrow door, no reliable power. Budget: 600 rand. Each fact cuts options: she can pull 150 newtons, so the machine needs advantage 3 or 4; no power, so hand-operated; children, so the load must never fall. Split the job: lift, move, input, guide. Table the mechanisms from this term: tackle, jack, worm winch, rack, lever. For every hazard, a control. Then write a page. Now you are ready to design.
visual_style: Whiteboard list of facts filling in; a quick calculation 500 / 150; a table with tackle, jack, winch rows; hazard-control pairs appearing; a closed sketchbook with a tick.
mood: Methodical and encouraging, like a planning meeting.
pacing: Facts, cuts, split, table, hazards, page.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write the five facts for a lifting problem in your own home.
